statement: Let S = C0(Y ) ⊗ P, and prescribe countably many pairs xl ∈ S+, el ∈ J(Uxl ), l ∈ N. There is a homomorphism θ : S → D satisfying θ(S(U)) ⊆ J(U), el ∈ IdealD(θ(xl)) (U ⊆ X open, l ∈ N), (4.1) 20 in either of the following situations. (i) An existing model χ : S → D is given. In this case θ can be a slowly vanishing rational UHF fraction of χ, and it also satisfies θ(S(Ux)) ⊆ IdealD(θ(x)) (x ∈ S+). (4.2) For every fixed N, N copies of its defining fraction fit in the defining copy of χ at all sufficiently late coordinates. (ii) Y = (0, 1]. No model is needed in this case, and (4.2) is not asserted. In both cases, for every l and ε > 0 there is δl,ε > 0 such that [(|el| − ε)+] ≤ [(θ(xl) − δl,ε)+] in Cu(D). (4.3) The construction permits the prescribed errors and the stabilizer to occupy separate matrix corners.
